Mercimek Çorbası (Red Lentil Soup)

35 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — The Pul Biber & Mint Tarka

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Red lentils60g120g180g240g
Onion, chopped20g40g60g80g
Carrot, chopped20g40g60g80g
Potato, chopped30g60g90g120g
Garlic clove½11½2
Tomato paste5g10g15g20g
Ground cumin⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Paprika⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Chicken or vegetable stock250ml500ml750ml1000ml
Olive oil5ml10ml15ml20ml
Butter (for the tarka)5g10g15g20g
Dried mint⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Pul biber (Aleppo pepper flakes)⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Saltpinch¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Lemon wedges1234

Steps

  1. Warm the olive oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the onion and carrot and cook 4-5 minutes until softened.
  2. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
  3. Stir in the tomato paste, cumin, and paprika, cooking 1 minute until deep red and fragrant.
  4. Add the red lentils, potato, and stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 20-25 minutes until completely soft.
  5. Blend the soup until smooth and velvety, using an immersion blender or a standard blender in batches.
  6. Return to low heat, thin with a splash of water or stock if needed, and season with salt.
  7. Make the tarka: melt the butter in a small pan, add the dried mint and pul biber, and sizzle 20-30 seconds until fragrant.
  8. Ladle into bowls, drizzle the mint-pul biber butter on top, and serve with lemon wedges.

Turkish Köfte with Rice Pilaf

35 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Shaping the Köfte

Köfte — Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Ground beef (or beef & lamb mix)120g240g360g480g
Onion, grated20g40g60g80g
Garlic clove, grated½11½2
Dried breadcrumbs10g20g30g40g
Ground cumin⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Paprika⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Dried oregano⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Parsley, chopped5g10g15g20g
Black pepper⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Olive oil (for searing)10ml20ml30ml40ml

Rice Pilaf — Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Baldo or long-grain rice60g120g180g240g
Orzo (şehriye)10g20g30g40g
Butter10g20g30g40g
Olive oil5ml10ml15ml20ml
Chicken stock120ml240ml360ml480ml
Saltpinch¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp

Steps

  1. In a bowl, combine the ground beef, grated onion, garlic, breadcrumbs, cumin, paprika, oregano, parsley, salt, and pepper. Mix and knead briefly until well combined.
  2. Shape into oval or flattened round patties about the size of your palm. Rest 10 minutes in the fridge if time allows.
  3. Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
  4. Sear the köfte 3-4 minutes per side until deeply browned and cooked through with no pink in the center.
  5. Meanwhile, make the pilaf: melt the butter with the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the orzo and toast 1-2 minutes until golden brown.
  6. Add the rice and stir to coat every grain in the fat, toasting 1-2 minutes more.
  7. Pour in the hot chicken stock and salt, bring to a boil, then cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
  8. Remove from heat, keep covered, and let rest 5-10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
  9. Serve the köfte hot alongside the rice pilaf.

Karnıyarık (Stuffed Eggplant with Ground Beef)

55 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — The Split & Stuffed Eggplant

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Eggplants, medium1234
Ground beef100g200g300g400g
Onion, chopped30g60g90g120g
Garlic cloves, minced1234
Green pepper, chopped½11½2
Tomatoes, diced1234
Tomato paste10g20g30g40g
Red pepper paste (biber salçası)5g10g15g20g
Parsley, chopped5g10g15g20g
Ground cumin⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Saltpinch¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Black pepper⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Olive oil (for frying)40ml80ml120ml160ml
Water or stock30ml60ml90ml120ml
Tomato slices (for topping)2468

Steps

  1. Peel the eggplants in alternating strips, then slit each lengthwise down the middle without cutting all the way through.
  2. Salt the eggplants and let sit 15 minutes to draw out bitterness, then rinse and pat dry.
  3. Shallow-fry the eggplants in olive oil over medium heat, turning, until softened and lightly golden all over, 8-10 minutes. Arrange in a baking dish, gently pressing open the slit.
  4. Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
  5. In the same pan, cook the onion 3-4 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and green pepper, cooking 2 minutes more.
  6. Add the ground beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned with no pink remaining.
  7. Stir in the tomato paste and red pepper paste, cooking 1 minute until deep red and fragrant.
  8. Add the diced tomatoes, cumin, parsley, salt, and pepper, and simmer 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
  9. Spoon the meat filling generously into the slit of each eggplant, mounding it on top.
  10. Top each stuffed eggplant with a tomato slice and a strip of green pepper. Pour the water or stock into the bottom of the baking dish.
  11. Bake 20-25 minutes until the eggplant is fully tender and the filling is bubbling.
  12. Serve hot, with rice pilaf and yogurt on the side if you like.

Tavuk Şiş (Chicken Shish Kebab)

25 min (+1 hr marinate)MediumServes 1–4

Prep — Grilled Chicken Şiş, Plated

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken thighs, boneless & skinless, cubed130g260g390g520g
Plain yogurt30g60g90g120g
Olive oil10ml20ml30ml40ml
Tomato paste5g10g15g20g
Garlic clove, grated½11½2
Paprika⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Ground cumin⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Pul biber (Aleppo pepper flakes)⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Dried oregano⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Saltpinch¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Bell pepper (for skewers)¼½¾1
Cherry tomatoes (for skewers)2468
Red onion, thinly sliced20g40g60g80g
Sumac⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Lemon wedges1234

Steps

  1. In a bowl, whisk together the yogurt, olive oil, tomato paste, garlic, paprika, cumin, pul biber, oregano, salt, and pepper.
  2. Add the cubed chicken and toss until every piece is coated. Cover and marinate in the fridge at least 1 hour.
  3. Thread the marinated chicken onto skewers, alternating with pieces of bell pepper and cherry tomatoes.
  4. Heat a grill, grill pan, or broiler to high heat.
  5. Grill the skewers 10-12 minutes total, turning every few minutes, until deeply charred in spots and cooked through with no pink at the center.
  6. While the chicken grills, toss the sliced red onion with sumac and a pinch of salt for a quick onion salad.
  7. Serve the skewers hot with the sumac onion salad and lemon wedges for squeezing over.

Turkish Chicken Güveç (Chicken & Vegetable Stew)

55 min (mostly hands-off)EasyServes 1–4

Prep — Meat & Vegetables in the Güveç Pot

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken thighs, boneless & skinless, chunked130g260g390g520g
Onion, sliced30g60g90g120g
Garlic cloves1234
Red bell pepper, chopped¼½¾1
Green bell pepper, chopped¼½¾1
Potato, chopped60g120g180g240g
Tomatoes, chopped½11½2
Tomato paste5g10g15g20g
Red pepper paste (biber salçası)5g10g15g20g
Bay leaf¼½¾1
Dried oregano⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Dried mintpinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp
Saltpinch¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Black pepper⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Olive oil10ml20ml30ml40ml
Water or stock60ml120ml180ml240ml

Steps

  1. Warm the olive oil in a wide pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chicken and sear 3-4 minutes until lightly golden.
  2. Add the onion and garlic, cooking 3-4 minutes until softened.
  3. Stir in the tomato paste and red pepper paste, cooking 1 minute until fragrant.
  4. Add the bell peppers, potato, tomatoes, bay leaf, oregano, dried mint, salt, and pepper.
  5. Pour in the water or stock, stir well, and bring to a gentle simmer.
  6. Cover and simmer on low heat 35-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is fully cooked and potatoes are tender.
  7. Uncover and simmer 5-10 more minutes to thicken the sauce slightly.
  8. Discard the bay leaf, taste and adjust seasoning, then serve hot with crusty bread.

Lahmacun (Turkish Flatbread with Spiced Meat)

50 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Rolling & Baking a Batch

Dough — Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Bread or all-purpose flour70g140g210g280g
Instant yeast⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Warm water40ml80ml120ml160ml
Olive oil5ml10ml15ml20ml
Saltpinch¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp

Topping — Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Ground lamb or beef80g160g240g320g
Onion, finely chopped30g60g90g120g
Tomato, finely chopped½11½2
Garlic clove½11½2
Parsley, finely chopped10g20g30g40g
Tomato paste5g10g15g20g
Red pepper paste (biber salçası)5g10g15g20g
Paprika⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Pul biber⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Ground cumin⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp

Steps

  1. Make the dough: dissolve the yeast in the warm water and let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
  2. Combine the flour and salt in a bowl, add the yeast water and olive oil, and knead 5-6 minutes until smooth and elastic.
  3. Cover and let rise in a warm spot 20-25 minutes until slightly puffy.
  4. Meanwhile, finely chop the onion, tomato, garlic, and parsley together until they form a wet, finely minced paste.
  5. Combine this vegetable mixture with the ground lamb, tomato paste, red pepper paste, paprika, pul biber, cumin, salt, and pepper.
  6. Preheat the oven as hot as it goes (240-260°C / 465-500°F) with a baking sheet or pizza stone inside.
  7. Divide the dough into portions and roll each one out very thin, almost paper-thin, on a floured surface.
  8. Spread a thin, even layer of the meat topping all the way to the edges of each dough round.
  9. Transfer the topped rounds onto the hot baking sheet and bake 7-9 minutes until the edges are crisp and the meat is fully cooked.
  10. Serve immediately, rolled up with a squeeze of lemon, fresh parsley, and sliced onion inside.

Turkish Pide (Cheese & Beef Flatbread)

60 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Kıymalı Pide Fresh from the Oven

Dough — Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Bread flour90g180g270g360g
Instant yeast⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Warm water50ml100ml150ml200ml
Plain yogurt10g20g30g40g
Olive oil5ml10ml15ml20ml
Sugarpinch¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Saltpinch¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp

Filling — Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Ground beef60g120g180g240g
Onion, finely chopped20g40g60g80g
Green pepper, chopped¼½¾1
Tomato, chopped¼½¾1
Tomato paste5g10g15g20g
Red pepper paste (biber salçası)5g10g15g20g
Shredded kaşar cheese (or mozzarella)40g80g120g160g
Paprika⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Pul biberpinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp
Egg (for egg wash)¼½¾1
Butter, melted (to finish)5g10g15g20g

Steps

  1. Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm water; let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
  2. Mix in the yogurt, olive oil, flour, and salt, and knead 6-8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
  3. Cover and let rise in a warm place 45-60 minutes until roughly doubled.
  4. Meanwhile, mix the ground beef, onion, green pepper, tomato, tomato paste, red pepper paste, paprika, pul biber, salt, and pepper to make the filling.
  5. Preheat the oven to 230°C (450°F) with a baking sheet inside.
  6. Punch down the dough and roll each portion into a long oval, about 1cm thick.
  7. Spread the meat filling down the center, leaving a 2-3cm border, and sprinkle the shredded kaşar cheese over the filling.
  8. Fold the two long edges of the dough up and over the filling, pinching the ends together to form a boat shape.
  9. Brush the exposed crust with beaten egg for shine.
  10. Bake 12-15 minutes until the crust is deep golden and the filling is bubbling and cooked through.
  11. Brush the hot crust with melted butter as soon as it comes out of the oven, then slice and serve.

Sütlaç (Turkish Rice Pudding) (Bonus)

45 min (+2 hr chill)EasyServes 1–4

Prep — Under the Broiler

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Short or medium-grain rice15g30g45g60g
Water (to par-cook rice)60ml120ml180ml240ml
Whole milk200ml400ml600ml800ml
Sugar20g40g60g80g
Cornstarch5g10g15g20g
Vanilla extract¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Egg yolk (optional, for richness)¼½¾1
Ground cinnamon (for topping)pinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp

Steps

  1. Rinse the rice and simmer it in the water over low heat, covered, 10-12 minutes until just tender.
  2. Add the milk and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring occasionally so the rice doesn't stick.
  3. Whisk the cornstarch with a splash of cold milk until smooth, then stir this slurry into the pot.
  4. Add the sugar and simmer 10-15 minutes, stirring frequently, until thickened to a pourable custard consistency.
  5. Temper the egg yolk with a spoonful of the hot mixture, then stir it back into the pot (optional — the pudding sets from the cornstarch alone).
  6. Stir in the vanilla extract and simmer 2 more minutes.
  7. Pour the pudding into individual ramekins or bowls.
  8. For the traditional caramelized top, place under a hot broiler 2-3 minutes until brown spots form — or skip and simply dust with cinnamon.
  9. Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate at least 2 hours until fully chilled and set.
  10. Sprinkle with ground cinnamon just before serving.
